summary: No held thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Every single-stock holding (CARG, DPZ, IDXX, INCY, KR, MSCI, SAM, VRSN) is still on the screen menu (dated 2026-11-17) with CFO above net income, its F-score unchanged from its stored thesis, no flags, and every stop block 'ok' at the close. TLT is the only holding off the menu, which is expected for a bond ETF. The two equity sales today were not fundamental breaks. WMT was sold on its stored XLP clause while still on the menu at F7, gp_sector_pct 0.863 and CFO $41.6B against NI $21.9B. IDXX was trimmed for beta and sector reasons while still F8, gp_sector_pct 0.942 and CFO $1,181.8M against NI $1,059.5M. No lesson in learning.json names the fundamentals-analyst and I have no graded calls, so neither shaped this review.
update: 1) Thesis text that is still stale after today's thesis_updates: SAM's stored thesis still says it 'joins WMT and KR in the Staples bucket inside the same factor', but WMT was sold today, and KR's updated thesis already says KR and SAM are the Staples bucket. SAM should be restated to match. IDXX's new line 'Executives sold over $27M of stock after the run' has no date or run named, so it will be unreadable at the next run. TLT's stop text still points to the $80.75 fill of 11-20. Its blended cost after today's $81.11 add is a little higher, so the 'about 5.5%' figure has to be restated from that cost at the next run, as the text itself says. 2) Exposure by SIC label: DPZ (11.9%), KR (5.7%) and SAM (2.3%) come to about 20% of equity labelled Consumer Staples. Of that, DPZ is the wholesale-groceries mislabel (bucket Consumer Discretionary). So by business, the Staples sleeve is now about 8% after the WMT sale. CARG's menu label is Technology while its thesis files it as Communication by bucket. The bucket fits an online auto marketplace better, and both sectors are on the Market Analyst's avoid list per the PM, so the label does not change today's call. 3) The menu-based clauses in DPZ ('screen drops it from the menu or shows CFO below net income') and SAM ('screen drops SAM from the menu') are both untripped. The menu is dated 11-17, four sessions old, so these clauses cannot trip again until the screen is refreshed. 4) The fundamentals are aging. Every held single stock except KR (FY to 2026-01-31) reports on a fiscal year that ended in late December 2025, about 11 months ago. The next 10-Ks are due around February 2027, the same window as most held names' next earnings (IDXX 2027-02-01, VRSN 2027-02-04, INCY 2027-02-09, CARG 2027-02-18, DPZ 2027-02-22, SAM 2027-02-23). The F-scores therefore say nothing about 2026 so far, which is why the quarterly prints and guidance clauses matter more than the screen for these names. 5) Sleeve-level accounting notes still apply: DPZ and MSCI both fail leverage_not_up, and KR fails roa_improved and current_ratio_improved (F7, the lowest score held). None is new, and none is a reason to sell on its own. 6) Non-fundamental items in the files on held names were already judged by the PM and are not thesis breaks: KR's Grubhub sounding-out (no bid or 8-K) and its CRFB baby-food report, SAM's planned CEO handover, and insider sales at DPZ, IDXX, INCY and VRSN. KR's 12-03 print is the next fundamental test, and a Grubhub deal would be a capital-allocation question there.
